lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: There — Menippus here will judge which of us is better-looking. Tell me, Menippus, don't I seem the handsomer to you?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Well, who are you, first? I think I ought to know that before anything else.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And which is Nireus, and which is Thersites? Because that part isn't obvious yet.

lines.speaker: Thersites
lines.text: There — that's one point to me already. I look just like you, and you don't have anything like the advantage that blind old Homer gave you when he called you the handsomest man of them all. No — pinhead and patchy-haired as I am, I came out no worse in the judge's eyes. Go on then, Menippus — say which of us you think the better-looking.

lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: Me, obviously — son of Aglaia and Charops, the handsomest man who came to Troy.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Yes, but you didn't come down here the handsomest, did you? The bones are identical. The only way I could tell your skull from Thersites' is that yours is the more brittle of the two — a flimsy thing, not what I'd call a man's skull.

lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: Well, ask Homer what I was like, back when I went on campaign with the Achaeans.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: You're telling me dreams. I look at what you've got now. What you used to have — that's a matter for the people who were there.

lines.speaker: Nireus
lines.text: So I'm not the handsomer down here, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Neither you nor anyone else is handsome. In Hades it's one rate for everyone. [pause] You all look the same.

lines.speaker: Thersites
lines.text: Well — that's good enough for me.
